notes.meaning: Speaking gently can calm someone's burning rage, while harsh words make tempers flare up like a fire. A quiet, soft reply disarms hostility and protects peace. Responding to anger with anger only makes things worse.

Wise people know how to use their knowledge well, sharing good teaching at the right time and place. In contrast, fools babble on without thinking, pouring out nonsense that helps no one. Good speech builds others up instead of showing off.

God sees everything that happens across the whole earth, watching both good and bad actions. Nothing can be hidden from Him, not even secret sins or quiet acts of service. This gives comfort to those doing right and warns those doing wrong.

Gentle and soothing speech brings healing, refreshing others like fruit from a tree of life. On the other hand, deceitful and cruel talk crushes the human spirit and causes deep wounds. Our words have the power either to comfort hearts or break them.

A person who brushes off a father's guidance acts foolishly and heads toward trouble. Someone who takes correction to heart shows good sense and learns how to live well. Accepting loving reproof is a mark of true wisdom.

Upright living brings lasting blessings into a home, whether in material goods or spiritual contentment. The profits of the wicked, however, come wrapped in anxiety, guilt, and turmoil. True wealth includes peace of mind that ungodly gain can never buy.

Wise people freely share helpful truth with others, spreading understanding wherever they go. Fools cannot do this because their hearts are crooked and have no store of wisdom to give. What comes out of a person's mouth shows what fills the heart.

Outward religious rituals mean nothing to the Lord when offered by people who stubbornly cling to wickedness. God despises insincere sacrifices, but He genuinely delights in the humble, honest prayers of the upright. He looks at the state of the heart, not just external ceremonies.

The Lord hates the whole daily conduct and lifestyle of those who practice evil. In contrast, He dearly loves those who make it their steady goal to live righteously. God cares about the path someone walks every day, not just occasional good deeds.

Severe punishment awaits anyone who wanders off the right path and leaves God's way. Those who refuse correction and hate being rebuked will ultimately face destruction and death. Turning away from discipline puts a person's life in serious danger.

Even the deepest realm of the dead and destruction lies completely exposed to God's sight. If the hidden depths of the grave cannot hide from Him, the secret thoughts and motives of human hearts are even more obvious to Him. God understands every person completely.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars view Sheol as simply a shadowy underworld where all the dead dwell, rather than the place of punishment known in later Christian theology.

notes.meaning: A proud mocker refuses to listen to correction and dislikes anyone who points out a fault. Because such a person hates being told what is wrong, he avoids spending time with wise teachers. Mockers would rather stay ignorant than admit they need to change.

A glad and cheerful heart brightens a person's face, making them pleasant to be around. But deep inner sorrow and distress break a person's spirit and sap their strength. Our inner spiritual and emotional health directly affects how we face daily life.

People with good sense are always hungry to learn more, seeking out knowledge so they can grow. Fools, however, feed on empty chatter and silly ideas, finding their satisfaction in foolishness. What our minds crave shows whether we are wise or foolish.

For someone burdened by constant sorrow and affliction, every day feels heavy and bitter. But a person with a cheerful, contented heart experiences life as if sitting at a continuous banquet. Joy grounded in God provides an inner feast no outward trouble can destroy.

Having just a little food and modest possessions while honoring the Lord is far better than owning huge wealth accompanied by constant anxiety and strife. Reverence for God brings a calm conscience that money cannot provide. Peace of mind is greater than mountains of riches.

A simple meal of plain vegetables eaten where people genuinely love one another is far more enjoyable than a feast of prime meat served with bitterness and hatred. Love sweetens the humblest table, while conflict ruins the finest banquet. Warm relationships matter far more than luxury.

An angry, quick-tempered person quickly starts arguments and sets communities into conflict. A patient person who controls their anger cools down disputes and restores calm. Patience acts like water on the flames of quarreling.

A lazy person imagines roadblocks and thorns at every step, making excuses to avoid honest work. But the upright person works diligently, finding that duty turns into a smooth, clear highway. Willing effort removes imaginary obstacles from our path.

A child who behaves wisely brings deep gladness to a father's heart. A foolish person treats an aging mother with disrespect, showing both ingratitude and an utter lack of sense. Honoring parents is a clear sign of godly wisdom.

A person without good judgment actually enjoys doing foolish and sinful things. Someone with understanding, however, stays on the straight path and lives by God's truth. Finding pleasure in wickedness is a sure sign of a foolish heart.

When people rush ahead without asking for advice, their plans often fall apart. But when they seek guidance from many trusted counselors, their plans are much more likely to succeed. Wise planning requires the humility to listen to others.

A person finds real joy in giving the right answer when someone needs help. A helpful word spoken at the exact right moment is a wonderful gift to the hearer. God honors speech that is both thoughtful and well-timed.

The path of wisdom leads a person upward toward life and keeps them away from death and the grave below. Wise choices protect someone from the destructive traps that ruin ungodly lives. Living in obedience to God sets a person on a higher road.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars understand this verse to speak only of preserving one's physical life and avoiding an early death, rather than pointing to life in heaven after death.

notes.meaning: The Lord tears down the estates of arrogant people who think they can mistreat others without consequence. At the same time, He actively defends the property boundaries of vulnerable widows who have no earthly protector. God opposes the proud and stands up for the helpless.

The Lord hates wicked schemes and evil motives formed in the secret thoughts of human hearts. In contrast, words that are pure, kind, and friendly bring Him genuine delight. God cares as much about our inner attitudes as our spoken words.

A person driven by dishonest greed brings chaos, worry, and a curse upon his entire household. But someone who refuses bribes and rejects dishonest gain will enjoy life and safety. Chasing dirty money always harms the family it was meant to enrich.

Righteous people pause and think carefully before speaking, making sure their words are helpful and true. Wicked people blurt out whatever comes into their heads, pouring forth harmful and careless speech. Self-control over the tongue is a true mark of godliness.

The Lord remains far from the wicked because their stubborn sin keeps them separated from His favor. Yet He stays close to righteous people and attentively hears their sincere prayers. God welcomes those who seek to obey Him.

A cheerful look from a friend brings warmth and happiness to the heart. In the same way, receiving good news brings deep relief and restores strength to the whole body. Kind gestures and encouraging words have power to revive weary spirits.

Anyone who willingly listens to life-giving correction will find a lasting home among the wise. Instead of resenting a rebuke, such a person learns from it and grows in wisdom. Being open to advice places us in the company of those who live well.

A person who turns away from correction shows that he cares little for his own soul and future. But whoever takes reproof to heart gains understanding and guards his life against ruin. Accepting instruction is the best way to care for oneself.

Reverence and awe toward the Lord is the true classroom of wisdom. Before a person can receive lasting honor, they must first learn to walk in genuine humility. God lifts up those who are willing to humble themselves before Him.
